evals.prompt: Draft an issue to add a pomodoro timer UI to task cards in StudyBuddy+. The timer should support normal and pomodoro modes. Note that the backend already has the timer endpoints (POST /api/tasks/{id}/timer/start and POST /api/tasks/{id}/timer/stop) — only the frontend UI needs to be built.
evals.expected_output: A well-formed markdown issue draft in issues/ that follows the exact required format: H1 title starting with a verb, User Story, Description, Acceptance Criteria (checkboxes), Technical Notes with Frontend/Backend/Database/Dependencies rows, and Testing Considerations.
expectations: The draft contains an H1 title that starts with 'Add', 'Implement', or 'Build'
The draft contains a '## User Story' section with 'As a', 'I want', and 'so that' lines
The draft contains an '## Acceptance Criteria' section with at least 3 checkbox items
The draft contains a '## Technical Notes' section with Frontend changes, Backend changes, Database, and Dependencies rows
The draft contains a '## Testing Considerations' section with unit tests, integration tests, and edge cases
Frontend changes are listed as non-None (UI work is required)
Backend changes are listed as None or note existing endpoints (no new backend work required)
The draft is saved to a file in the issues/ directory

evals.prompt: Create an issue to fix a bug where the task status filter on the StudyBuddy+ dashboard shows incorrect results — selecting 'in-progress' still displays tasks marked as 'done'.
evals.expected_output: A bug-fix issue draft with a Fix-prefixed title, clear acceptance criteria describing correct filter behavior, frontend-focused technical notes, and edge case testing considerations.
expectations: The draft contains a '## User Story' section
The draft contains an '## Acceptance Criteria' section with checkboxes describing the correct filter behavior
The draft contains a '## Technical Notes' section identifying the frontend filter component
The draft contains a '## Testing Considerations' section that mentions edge cases like empty filter results
The draft is saved to a file in the issues/ directory
